sources.title: The Town Hall 17 Update Is Here!
sources.finding: Describes aimed defenses such as Air Sweeper as having a player-selected aim direction and a covered cone. It does not publish Air Sweeper range, cadence, cone angle, push distance, collision, target choice or state-transition timing.

sources.title: Air Sweeper | Clash of Clans Wiki | Goblins Farm
sources.finding: Reports 2x2 geometry, seven levels, no damage, air-only support role and two units available at TH18; it states that its values are from client build 18.400.21, which predates the frozen TH18 reference. It supplies no numerical blast geometry, cadence, push path or deterministic targeting rule.

sources.title: Air Sweeper | Clash of Clans Wiki | Fandom
sources.finding: Lists push strengths 1.6–4.0 tiles by level, 1–15 range, 5-second attack speed, air-only targeting and repeated directional pushback. Its own descriptions conflict on coverage geometry (90-degree target arc, 120-degree sector/30-degree blast, and 60-degree effect), and it does not define blast origin, precise push vector/path, collision clipping, multi-target order, interruption or retarget timing.

confirmed_qualitative_behavior: aim direction selected by the defender
findings.not_imported: No new value is imported into the frozen catalogue or Core because the secondary numeric source has no game version and disagrees internally on cone geometry; the dated-build source predates the target reference and lacks the mechanics values.
blocking_unknowns: current-version blast cone geometry and origin
ordered multi-target selection and entity-ID ties
exact displacement vector, collision/path clipping and wall interaction
attack interruption, immobilization and retarget timing
findings.next_evidence: A version-identified client-data record plus reproducible, tick-aligned battle captures covering cone edges, multiple equal candidates, collision boundaries, target loss and snapshot/replay restoration.

conclusion: The post-freeze audit adds evidence to an open mechanics record only. It preserves the 2026-09-17 reference unchanged and does not authorize a generic damage weapon or inferred pushback implementation.
